info.title: APEX: paid web reads and on-chain data for agents (x402, USDC)
info.summary: Pay-per-call reads for agents: rendered web pages, page to markdown, token and NFT info, plus Arc, Base and X1 on-chain data (exit checks, contract powers, agent registry health).
info.description: Reads sold per call over x402, built for agents. Web: a real headless-Chrome page extractor, a page as markdown, a plain web read, a page snapshot. Tokens: token and NFT info. On-chain data: Arc (Circle's L1, eip155:5042): about 9 in 10 new USDC-paired Uniswap v4 launches (Argus included), each with a simulated buy-then-sell verdict (no money moves), exit checks, hook risk, deployer history, ERC-8004 agent liveness and payability. Base: exit checks (a simulated buy and full sell), gas cost in dollars, Basenames. Arc and Base: contract owner powers, one-sentence transaction explanations. X1: token, pool, trade, wallet and exit-liquidity data. The free claim stays on the site. An unpaid call returns a standard x402 402 listing every rail: USDC on Arc (EIP-3009 authorization we settle, or Circle Gateway nanopayments), USDC on Base (same two), USDC on Solana, USD1 or U on BNB Chain, USDG on Robinhood Chain (both EIP-3009, we settle and pay the gas; minimum $0.01), or XNT on X1. Pay the payTo that the 402 names for your network. Free discovery: /.well-known/x402 and /api/x402/discovery.
info.x-guidance:
What this is: paid GET endpoints under https://apexfaucet.xyz/api/x402/. Each returns JSON wrapped as {ok, paid, tier, data}.
How to pay: call once without payment, read the 402 (v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED header, v1 JSON accepts[]), pick your network, sign, repeat the call with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. On Arc and Base, Circle Gateway balances work (gasless). A call we cannot serve (missing or malformed parameter) is refused before payment.
When to call what:
- Read a web page an ordinary fetch returns empty: /api/x402/page-extract?url=... ($0.009, real Chrome, JavaScript executed). A whole docs site in one call: /api/x402/site-extract?url=... ($0.14).
- Before buying a new Arc token: /api/x402/arc-fresh ($0.003) lists recent launches, each with a sell verdict from a simulated buy-then-sell about 12 s after the pool opened (verdictAgeSeconds says how old; re-check liquidity if verdictStale) and a bundle verdict once its first two minutes are read (bundle.verdict). Polling? Pass since=<nextSince from your last answer> to get only new launches; limit=N for the newest N.
- One Arc pool, buy or not: /api/x402/arc-verdict?pool=<v4 pool id> or ?token=0x... ($0.002). Up to 25 at once: /api/x402/arc-exit-check-bulk ($0.025).
- Was a launch bundled (creator's own buy, wallets it funded buying first): /api/x402/arc-bundle?token=0x... or ?pool=... ($0.004).
- Hook risk from the hook address alone, no chain call: /api/x402/arc-hook-risk?hook=0x... ($0.003).
- Is an Arc agent alive and payable: /api/x402/arc-agent-watch ($0.004). Did a payment land: /api/x402/arc-payment?tx=0x... or /api/x402/x1-payment?sig=... ($0.003).
- Base: can you sell this token, and at what loss: /api/x402/base-exit-check/0x<token> ($0.01). Gas cost in dollars: /api/x402/base-gas ($0.001, Base only).
- Arc or Base contract, what can its owners do to holders: /api/x402/contract-flags?chain=base|arc&address=0x... ($0.004). What a transaction did: /api/x402/tx-explain?chain=base|arc&tx=0x... ($0.003).
- X1 tokens: /api/x402/token/{mint}, /holders/{mint}, /trades/{mint} ($0.003); sell-side exit check /api/x402/exit-check/{mint} ($0.004).
Every verdict is a measurement at a stated time, not a promise. Prices are in USD; the 402 is authoritative. Full list: /.well-known/x402.

get.summary: Check a payee before paying: Pay-safe: one EIP-712 PaySafeVerdict before you send USDC. Pass ?payee=<0x>. Optional &chain=arc|base (default arc), &payer=<0x>, &amount= (a USDC decimal like 0.01, or atomic units such as 9000 only when resource and nonce are set), &resource=<https URL>, &nonce=<0x and 64 hex>, &window= seconds. The verdict covers the payee (Arc poison index, lookalikes, USDC blacklist, and the OFAC SDN file; Base is the USDC blacklist on chain, and a missing lookalike index is CAUTION), a duplicate fingerprint when resource, nonce and amount are all present, our own catalog price, and whether that endpoint has a prior delivered settlement. Codes: payee NO_MATCH CAUTION DO_NOT_PAY COULD_NOT_READ; duplicate FRESH DUPLICATE NOT_CHECKED COULD_NOT_RECORD; price MATCH HIGH LOW UNKNOWN; delivered YES NO UNKNOWN. Verdict PASS only when every code is clean, else DO_NOT_PAY (bad payee, duplicate, or a price above our catalog), COULD_NOT_READ, or CAUTION. Domain APEX PaySafe version 1 chainId 5042. networkId in the message is 5042 or 8453. PayGuard does not read this type. This is not a permission to pay. 20 free a day at /pay-safe. This route is $0.01. A missing nonce is NOT_CHECKED and cannot be a PASS. The hook is /pay-safe/apex-pay-safe.js.

402.description: Payment required. This product is paid in USDC on Base, USDC on Arc or USDC on Solana only: the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header (v2) and the body list only that; sign the EIP-3009 authorization into PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and we settle it gaslessly, or pay and replay the hash (X-PAYMENT-BASE on Base, X-PAYMENT-ARC on Arc). A payment on any other chain is refused before it is settled. The $5 card pass (X-APEX-PASS) and $FAUCET holder access also work.

get.summary: Arc payee check: address poisoni: Call this before any USDC send on Arc. We index every Arc USDC transfer: in the 7 days to 3 Nov 2026 there were 134 address-poisoning events from 50 lookalike addresses against 105 wallets (live counts: /api/arc-poison-stats). Pass ?payee=<0x> (and &payer=<your wallet>&amount=<USDC> to catch lookalikes of your own counterparties and to use PayGuard). Returns an EIP-712 signed verdict: DO_NOT_PAY, CAUTION, NO_MATCH_IN_INDEX or COULD_NOT_READ, with the address it imitates, evidence transactions, the USDC blacklist and OFAC. 5 free a day at /api/arc-payee-check; unlimited here. PayGuard (0x942e886e4aa48346dd8bc594596f662aab57efeb on Arc) only pays on a clean, fresh verdict. A clean verdict that names the payer and the amount is an apex-upto-v1 voucher: the same signature, a cap, 10 minutes, once. New boxes (arc-mandate-2, factory 0x91957bd6e6da2880bf49174eaa4b5d36627af9d3) pay only on a clean PayeeVerdict whose payer is the box. pay() uses a verdict once. x402 can reuse one unexpired verdict on each free daily slot, and the daily count still applies. Boxes from the v1 factory 0x69e444f722666e13e171181efe054a93e0976b26 do not read the verdict. The v2 factory and the v2 implementation are Sourcify exact matches. arc-send-guard folds the same check: DO_NOT_PAY is a stop, and the signed verdict is arc-payee-check. Our own payouts to an address a stranger chose (the X reward, jury pay, the hunter bounty, and buy-and-rate) refuse DO_NOT_PAY before USDC leaves. A first payment to a new address is still allowed.

post.summary: Arc agent passport: An ERC-8004 identity on Arc for the agent that pays, minted and handed to the paying wallet in one call. POST JSON {name, description, image?, services?: [{name: web|A2A|MCP|x402|ENS|DID|email, endpoint}]}. We write a correct registration file and host it, mint the identity on Arc's registry (0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432) and transfer it to the address that signed the payment, never to a typed address. Paid on Arc or Base only, because the identity has to land in an EVM wallet. The answer carries the agentId, both transaction hashes and the passport page. Endpoints are probed first: if none answers, the file says active:false rather than pretending. The agent is then checked every hour by the APEX Watchtower and gets a tower in Arc City. Free alternative for a wallet that can send its own transaction: POST https://apexfaucet.xyz/api/arc/passport/draft.

post.summary: X1 agent passport: An ERC-8004 identity on X1 for the agent that pays, registered and handed to the paying wallet in one call. POST JSON {name, description, image?, services?: [{name: web|A2A|MCP|x402|ENS|DID|email, endpoint}]}. We write a correct registration file and host it, register it on X1's 8004 Solana Agent Registry (EwwrAhfTVHFffa97DKXoMVTUqtaq5JTZVsyUyYwXtzXp), initialise its ATOM reputation stats and transfer the agent to the wallet that sent the XNT payment, never to a typed address; ownership is read back from X1 before the answer. Paid in XNT on X1 only, because the agent has to land in an X1 wallet. The answer carries the agent id (its Core asset), the three transaction signatures and the hosted file. Unpaid: a 402 with the price. Not funded yet: a 503 and nothing charged.

get.summary: New token launches on Arc: APEX. Default is the last 20 minutes, at most 40, or the 5 newest. full=1 is the archive. Arc fresh launches, REAL TIME, each with a sell verdict and a bundle verdict, including the Argus launchpad (measured 6 Oct 2026: 45 of 52 Argus launches in a 2-hour window were in the feed). About 9 in 10 new USDC-paired Uniswap v4 pools on Arc (94 of 107 in that window) are caught by a WebSocket on PoolManager Initialize and exit-checked ~12 s after they open (the watcher drops the oldest job when its queue passes 60), so you learn whether a launch can actually be sold before you buy it. Every item also carries now: the same simulation repeated every 5 min for 24 h on launches that sold at launch, so a pool whose liquidity was pulled later says LIQUIDITY GONE with lostAt, and comes back to since= pollers when it is found. Each verdict names its method: a real buy-then-sell round trip (the probe contract for native-USDC pools, a sequential eth_simulateV1 through the launchpad router for ERC-20-USDC pools), or "SELL NOT MEASURED" in the rare case only a quote was possible. We no longer publish a share of launches that cannot be sold: the 77.5% we quoted on 2026-09-17 was measured with a sell quote taken before any buy, which fails on most fresh pools whatever they are, and was withdrawn on 2026-09-22 (see /corrections/). Each launch also carries a bundle verdict (BUNDLED, DEV BUY, SUSPECT or NO BUNDLE SEEN), read from the first 60 swaps of its first two minutes and who funded the earliest 12 buyers, added once those two minutes can be read, with measuredAt; evidence per launch: /api/x402/arc-bundle. The free feed at /api/arc/fresh is the same data delayed 300 s (bundle verdicts after 30 min); this is the first-seconds window a snipe is decided in.

get.summary: Arc bundle check: dev buy, rug: Was this Arc launch bundled? Pass ?token=0x... or ?pool=<v4 pool id>. We read the launch transaction, the first 60 swaps of the first two minutes and where the earliest 12 buyers' USDC came from in the ~3 hours before: BUNDLED (the creator and wallets it funded, or wallets funded by one shared wallet, bought early), DEV BUY (the creator bought its own token, with its share of the supply, and no other linked wallet was seen; unlinked wallets may also have bought; on one Arc launchpad creators can take about 50% in the launch transaction itself), SUSPECT (several brand-new wallets in the launch block) or NO BUNDLE SEEN. Each traced early wallet comes back with its share of the supply, up to 5 of its funders and the transaction; the answer says when the window had more swaps than were read. Contracts that pay out sale proceeds (routers, the pool manager) are not counted as funding. Limits, stated in the answer: funding older than ~3 hours or through an exchange or bridge is not seen.

get.summary: Gas price on Arc, from receipts: What a transaction on Arc ACTUALLY costs, measured from real receipts rather than quoted from the docs. The companion to /api/x402/arc-cost, which prices a named operation at the current gas price: that one is the quote, this one is the measurement and the tail. The most repeated claim about Arc is that USDC-as-gas means predictable low fees. The low half is true; the predictable half does not survive measurement, and that is what you are buying. You get the full percentile spread of cost per transaction in USDC, the cost broken down by transaction kind (contract call, plain transfer, contract deploy), the base-fee distribution with the share of blocks sitting on the 20 gwei floor, and the complete sampling method. A fee is gasUsed times effectiveGasPrice over 1e18, because USDC is the native gas token and native values carry 18 decimals - effectiveGasPrice is what was actually paid, not a bid, so these are fees and not estimates. HOW THIS COULD BE WRONG, and what we do about it: consecutive recent blocks measure one moment - twelve of them showed a base fee of exactly 20 gwei at both min and max, which reads as a fixed price, while forty blocks spread across 500,000 found six above the floor and one at 202.67 gwei. So blocks are spread across the span, transactions are taken from throughout each block rather than off the top where the highest-priority traffic sits, blocksFailed and receiptsFailed are published, and a 99th percentile is REFUSED below 200 samples because a p99 from 55 receipts is one observation wearing a statistic name. Every count is in the response; read it there, not here.

get.summary: Arc EURC stablecoin data: The EURO rail on Arc, which nothing else reports. Circle EURC (0xbEf5f6d51CB62b58e6A8f77868681825C6fe21c1) is live on Arc and every other Arc data product, ours included until now, is about new launches and the people sniping them. You get every EURC transfer in the scanned window with from, to, amount, block and transaction, the full top-10 net receivers and senders, and the live counts in summary. WHAT A TRANSFER LOG IS NOT: issuance (from 0x0) and redemption (to 0x0) are Transfer events too, so they are counted separately in summary.mints and summary.burns and are NEVER inside summary.transferredEurc - an early version of this data had one 20,019 EURC mint sitting inside the moved total, which made its recipient look like the biggest receiver on the chain. Logs are de-duplicated on transaction and log index and summary reports how many duplicates were removed, so you can check it rather than trust it. method.rangesOk and method.rangesFailed are both published: a failed range is never served as a quiet chain. The window is the most recent ~4,000 blocks and it SLIDES, refreshed every ten minutes, so the transfer count and volume are different every time you call and no figure for them is quoted here on purpose. The supply is read from the contract on every scan and returned in token.totalSupply; it moves with issuance and redemption, so it is not quoted here either. Everything comes from token, summary and method in the response you are paying for.

get.summary: Arc launchpad fee vaults: Arc launchpad fee vaults: every vault holding USDC right now, with its creator, its token and the change we measured since our previous scan, largest first. Fees only accrue from real swaps and a wash trader pays them on both legs, so vault growth is a costly-to-fake measure of genuine trading, unlike reported volume. Balances are the creator share and only the creator can collect them: distribute() pays creator() and treasury() and pays its caller nothing. A balance is not evidence a vault is abandoned. Every figure is read from chain state, and the response carries the block count it was measured over.

get.summary: Arc token launch archive: Every token launch recorded by the Arc launchpad Portal, kept so you do not need to run an archive node. Public Arc JSON-RPC endpoints cap each getLogs call at 10,000 blocks and the official one rate-limits bursts (both measured 29 Sep), so rebuilding this history yourself takes hundreds of calls - that is the work this saves. This is NOT the only copy: archive nodes, explorers, indexers and Circle all hold the full history. It is a convenience, not a monopoly. Each row is the block, the token contract, the addresses the Portal emitted (including the fee vault) and the transaction. The response states how many launches are held (held) from block 21001113 onward, growing hourly, with any range we could not read recorded as a gap rather than hidden. One call returns the NEWEST 5,000 by default; ?limit= raises that to 50,000 and ?sinceBlock= pages through the rest, so the whole archive takes several calls. This is a record, not a feed: it says what launched and when, and nothing about whether any of it was worth buying - for that see /api/x402/arc-exit-check-bulk.

get.summary: Arc CCTP bridge cost: What it really costs to bring USDC into Arc over Circle CCTP, measured from arrivals rather than quoted. Every arrival we hold with its recipient, the amount credited, the fee CCTP took and the transaction, plus observed fees grouped by transfer size. Read from MintAndWithdraw on TokenMessengerV2 0x28b5a0e9C621a5BadaA536219b3a228C8168cf5d, whose event signature we verified by hashing it rather than assuming it, and filtered to the USDC contract on every single log. The cost is punishing at small size: measured 2026-09-17, one arrival received 0.500000 USDC after a 1.000000 USDC fee on 1.5 sent, which we confirmed independently from that transaction native transfer logs. These are fees we observed. We do not model or predict Circle fees and this is not a quote. A size bucket with fewer than 5 arrivals reports its count and no median rather than a number built on two rows.

get.summary: Arc dead pool list: The Arc pool graveyard, in full: every Uniswap v4 pool on Arc we measured above a lifetime volume floor (minVolumeUsdc), each with its pool id, its state (empty = zero liquidity at the moment of the read, or alive), its lifetime USDC volume, its fee and its hook. The counts live in summary (poolsMeasured, empty, alive, emptyPct, USDC volume through empty and live pools) and the time of the read in generatedAt. Empty means nothing can be sold into that pool right now at any price; anyone may add liquidity again later, and a token is only as dead as its best pool, so check every pool of a token before calling it dead. Lifetime volume is what a pool did over its life, not money in it now. Tokens are identified by contract address, never by symbol.

get.summary: Arc fake token list: Every token symbol on Arc that more than one contract is using, with how many contracts wear each name and the canonical address where we have verified one. EVERY COUNT LIVES IN summary (symbolsReused, poolsIndexed, worstSymbol, worstCount) and NO count is quoted here, on purpose: the Arc index grows fast enough that a figure written into this text is stale within hours. The index accumulates every pool we see from the date in indexSince, which the response states; it does not reach back before that. Canonical addresses are given where we have verified one - for example Circle genesis ARC at 0xA12Cd81d0f9988E3d60c4B6a0D52D368Ef3c788d, which Circle has said is not live or tradeable, so any contract trading as ARC is not it. We report what shares a name; we never call a contract a scam, because using a common symbol is not proof of intent. Counted across tokens seen in a pool on Arc, which is not every contract ever deployed.

get.summary: Arc token deployer history: Who launched what on Arc, and did any of it ever trade. Every creator in our index with more than one launchpad token, with each token, the fees its vault holds, and the risk flags its pools carry. Fees accrue only from REAL swaps, so what a creator launches have earned is expensive to fake: EVERY COUNT LIVES IN summary (vaultsIndexed, distinctCreators, creatorsWithMoreThanOneToken) and none is quoted here: our vault index grew from 80 to 120 repeat creators inside a single evening on 2026-09-17, so any figure written into this text would be wrong by the time you read it. What does NOT move is the finding, measured that evening: the busiest launcher on Arc held 127 tokens and 0.000594 USDC in fees, while the single top earner held 24,180.23 USDC across just 3 tokens. Volume of launches and money earned are close to unrelated, which is the whole point of reading fees instead of counting tokens. Caveats carried in every response: creator is the address the launchpad fee vault returns from creator(), which is authoritative for who owns those fees but is NOT proof of which address deployed the token contract; counts cover the vaults we have indexed, not every launch on Arc; and a token with no pool in our index contributes no risk flags, so a creator with few flags may simply be one we have seen less of. We report what was launched and what it earned. We never label anyone.

get.summary: Bulk email verification: Clean an email list: pass ?emails=a@b.com,c@d.com (up to 100 in one call) and get a verdict per address plus totals. A DNS lookup that fails returns unknown, never a guess.

get.summary: Arc token deep safety check: Deep immune check for one Arc token: four readings in one call, fused into one grade. EXIT: a real buy-then-sell round trip simulated on Arc (nothing spent), the pool fee, a dynamic-fee hook, and whether a plain wallet can pull the liquidity. CLUSTER: was the launch bundled (the launcher and wallets it funded buying in the first two minutes, with their share of supply). HOLDERS: every Transfer since the first mint replayed into balances, top-10 wallets and what the creator still holds. HISTORY: what the creator launched before and how many of those carry risk flags. GRADE: A/B healthy (A clean; B fair: sells, with a cost or a caveat), C watch, D sick, F infected, ? unproven; the worst level any reading reaches, with every reason named. A reading we could not take is listed in evidence.missing and never counts as clean: one missing side reading rules out A, two or more give C at best, a sell test that did not run gives ? (and is refused before payment). Each answer carries ageSeconds (results are reused for at most 90 s). Returns the full evidence and its sha256 evidenceHash (canonical JSON, keys sorted) so you can recompute it; the same hash is shown at https://apexfaucet.xyz/arc/immune/{token}. A bad address, a token with no Arc pool or a sell test that could not run is refused before payment. 10% of every paid check is recorded as owed to a People Pot (a public ledger at https://apexfaucet.xyz/api/people-pot; the pot contract is deployed on Arc at 0xed8615da5256c6bdc6040fa6ae1d9f22070c48b7 and funded separately in small amounts, so the owed total is a ledger of what we intend to fund, and nothing has been paid to people from it yet).

402.description: Payment required. This product is paid in USDC on Base or USDC on Solana only: the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header (v2) and the body list only that; sign the EIP-3009 authorization into PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and we settle it gaslessly, or pay and replay the hash (X-PAYMENT-BASE on Base, X-PAYMENT-ARC on Arc). get.summary: Crawl a website, lite (up to 5 pages as text): Render up to 5 pages of one site in a real browser and return each page as clean text. Same host only. robots.txt is obeyed. get.summary: x402 delivery receipt: Pass the transaction hash of a payment to APEX. The answer is read from our settlement ledger: DELIVERED when the payer got an HTTP success with a body, PAID_NOT_DELIVERED when the response was an error or empty, REFUNDED when that payment is already in the refund list, DELIVERY_UNKNOWN when we recorded the payment and not the response, NOT_IN_OUR_LEDGER when the hash is not a payment we wrote down. This call does not send a refund.

A bad address, an unknown or foreign token, or a page that does not answer is refused before payment.

get.summary: Fact check a claim on the live web (quotes checked word for word): Fact check and verify a claim on the live web, and every quote is checked word for word. Pass ?claim= (10 to 300 characters). We search the live web (Groq browser search; Wikipedia when web search is limited, named in engine.search), fetch the top pages ourselves and number their sentences; an AI judge (Groq gpt-oss-120b, else qwen3.8-27b or gpt-oss-20b) reads only those sentences and returns its choice by sentence number. Every quote is a whole sentence our code took word for word from the page as we fetched it. Verdict: supported, contradicted, mixed or not_found, and unverified when no sentence backs it (no quote, no verdict). Each quote has its link and site; independentSources counts the distinct sites; the pages read, the pages that could not be read and the searches made are listed. The verdict is written by an AI and can be wrong; the quotes are exact. When the engine is limited, a paying call is refused before payment.
